Grounded in the code, rules-resolvable means EXACTLY one of two things: bonusTags the roll can match (equipmentBonus/wieldBonusFor), or numeric effects.health/energy the spend can apply (consumeItem). An item with neither is inert — it can be carried and described and can never once change a roll or a state.

a consumable with no numeric effects is the sharpest form of the hollow item: consumeItem (inventory.js:224) DESTROYS the stack and returns {} — the player spends a real resource and provably nothing happens. usableCombatItems will not even offer it as a move.

arc.ccodeReconciled: CCODE-55 (2026-08-01): `pressure-numeric` (someNumeric over magnitude/value/strength/x/y) -> `pressure-concrete` (nonEmptyString), reconciled against the real corpus — the same check every rule in this file gets, and the same false-positive class as the creature `threat` field. Arc pressure is a STRING of prose, never an object with numeric sub-keys: the 5 authored arcs carry 'slow-building, vast', 'the deep clock', 'building', 'medium', 'slow-building', and generate.js stubEntity mints 'medium'. someNumeric flagged 5 of 5 authored arcs. The INTENT behind the rule is right and is preserved — an arc whose pressure is only a mood cannot drive — but that is a judgement about WORDS, so it lives in vagueMarkers.byType.arc (where Aevi put it) rather than in a numeric shape-check the data can never satisfy. If the net-vector ever grows a numeric push field, the rule comes back keyed to THAT field. `hinges-present` kept exactly as authored: 0 of 5 authored arcs are empty and stubEntity mints `hingeNpcs: []`, so it flags precisely the stubbed arcs it should.
arc.note: SNG-250 §3/§5 (Aevi 2026-08-01): the arc contract - arc generates today but had NO contract, so the born-whole gate didn't cover the one live generator (boot said so). Grounded in the real SNG-203 net-vector reads. A whole arc DRIVES (has a real pressure/tendency) and RESOLVES (ifIgnored/ifEngaged are its stakes).

theConcreteLayer: CCODE-55 (SNG-250 §3/§4): each contentType may declare a `concrete` array beside `topLevel`. `topLevel` answers SNG-250's WHOLE question (does every consumer-read field carry a value?); `concrete` answers its CONCRETE question (is that value a real thing the rules can ACT on, or a word?). Every rule is machine-checkable and code-grounded — no rule here encodes a judgement, only a fact the engine already relies on. Rule vocabulary: `enum` (value in the listed set), `everyInVocab` (every array member resolves in a named content vocab — `function_vocabulary.verbs` is the 24 VERBS flattened out of the 8 families, which is what an ability's `functions` array actually holds; the families are what those verbs RESOLVE TO, not what is authored), `nonEmptyArray`, `numberInRange`, `someNumeric` (an object has a numeric value at one of `keys`), `anyOf` (at least one nested rule holds), `impliesSomeNumeric` (when `whenField` is truthy, `field` must have a numeric value at one of `keys`). ONE gate reads this for every type — a new type declares its contract here and is gated without new gate code (SNG-250 §5).
lanes: SNG-250 §4 OWNERSHIP. CCode owns the MECHANICAL half of this file — which fields a consumer reads, their types, and the `concrete` rules above, every one traceable to a real read or a real clamp in HEAD. Aevi owns the SEMANTIC half — the per-type vague/concrete PROSE markers ('wants the forge her brother left' vs 'wants respect'), which no static rule can decide. Those markers are deliberately NOT invented here; the §3 semantic bar for npc/item/creature/skill is Aevi's to author, and the gate will read them from this same file when they land (a `vagueMarkers` array per type is the natural slot).
howTheSweepUsesThis: For each contentType, for each authored instance, assert every non-optional field here is PRESENT and (where typed) correctly TYPED. CRASH-severity missing = the build must fail (a consumer throws). EMPTY = fail (renders broken - the visible class). DEGRADED = warn (works but hollow - e.g. no image) unless Erik promotes it. The generator round-trip (§5c) runs its OUTPUT through this same map. Grows by incident: a new consumer.read that breaks on absence adds a line here + the sweep covers it.
provenance: Every field verified at origin by grepping the consumer code for X.subfield reads (2026-07-25): quest reads app.js~6070-6130/7291; npc reads gm.js (25x .name) + SNG-233 directive; location reads random_encounters.js/SNG-180; creature reads random_encounters.js. Non-speculative - if a field isn't read by a real consumer, it's NOT here (no bloat, the SNG-232 lesson).

vagueMarkers.note: AEVI (2026-08-01): the SEMANTIC concrete/vague layer CCode's gate waits on (CCODE-55 OQ4). A value that is ONLY one of these abstractions, with no concrete anchor (a named thing/place/person/action the world tracks), fails the concreteness bar. NOT a hard reject on its own - a WARN that the value is generic; combined with the machine-checkable `concrete` rules it gates. Per type because 'vague' differs by field.

npc.note: a want must name a SPECIFIC actable thing the world can act on. VAGUE: 'wants respect'. CONCRETE: 'wants the forge her brother left, and resents that Silas holds it'. The test: can an NPC ACT toward it, and can the world grant/deny it?
npc.fearsNote: a fear must be specific enough to DRIVE behavior. VAGUE: 'fears failure'. CONCRETE: 'fears the water rising to the second bench again, the way it did the year the mill flooded'.

quest.note: an objective/condition must be a CHECKABLE state. VAGUE: 'restore harmony'. CONCRETE: 'shut the reclamation ring's valve and confirm the downstream wells run clear'. The SNG-249 test: can the GM say yes/no from game state without reading a metaphor?

item.note: an item effect must be RULES-RESOLVABLE. VAGUE: 'hums with old power'. CONCRETE: 'heals 8 health' / 'grants the shadow-harm strike'. Resolves through the real hooks (bonusTags / effects.health/energy).

skill.note: a skill must map to a real FUNCTION family (HARM/RESTORE/PROTECT/KNOW/SHAPE/INFLUENCE/MOVE/SUSTAIN) with a tier + cost. VAGUE: 'channels the essence of the deep'. CONCRETE: 'HARM, tier 1, 4 energy - a shadow-flavored strike'.

creature.note: a creature's behavior must name what it DOES mechanically. VAGUE: 'attacks fiercely'. CONCRETE: 'opens with a lunge (chase-morph on a miss), presses when wounded, breaks at half health'.

arc.note: an arc's pressure must be a DIRECTIONAL force with named consequences (SNG-239 statable tremor). VAGUE: 'something stirs'. CONCRETE: 'the deep sites report tremors, and each week untended, one more well upstream goes bad'.

_notes.gateTier: SNG-250 §7a (Erik-decided): per-type gate tier. hard = a hollow one BREAKS play, EMPTY escalates toward reject (creature/skill/quest/encounter); soft = a thin one degrades but plays, EMPTY stays repair/warn (item/npc/location/arc). Read by the SAME gate - one field, not a parallel policy system. Severities per field unchanged.
